questions.question: Which type of operating system executes jobs in a sequence without user interaction?
questions.explanation: Batch processing systems group similar jobs together and execute them sequentially without user interaction. Jobs are collected and processed in batches to improve efficiency.

questions.question: What characteristic defines a hard real-time operating system?
options: Attempts to meet deadlines but can occasionally miss them
Must meet all timing deadlines without exception
questions.explanation: Hard real-time systems must meet all timing deadlines without exception. Missing a deadline can lead to system failure, such as in aircraft control systems or medical devices.

questions.question: Which operating system type allows multiple users to access the system simultaneously by rapidly switching between them?
questions.explanation: Time-sharing systems allow multiple users to access the system concurrently by rapidly switching the CPU between users. Each user gets a time slice, creating the illusion of dedicated access.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a distributed operating system?
options: To manage multiple processors in a single computer
To coordinate multiple independent computers as a single system
To support multiple users on one machine
To run multiple operating systems simultaneously
questions.explanation: Distributed operating systems coordinate multiple independent computers connected by a network, making them appear as a single coherent system to users. Resources are shared across the network transparently.

questions.question: Which type of operating system is specifically designed for devices with limited resources?
questions.explanation: Embedded operating systems are designed for devices with limited resources like memory, processing power, and energy. They are specialized for specific tasks in devices like routers, sensors, and appliances.

questions.question: What distinguishes a network operating system from a distributed operating system?
options: Network OS requires manual resource access, distributed OS provides transparency
Network OS is faster than distributed OS
questions.explanation: In a network OS, users are aware of networked resources and must explicitly access them. In a distributed OS, the system provides transparency, making multiple computers appear as one unified system.

questions.question: Which OS type is optimized for handling multiple concurrent requests from clients?
questions.explanation: Server operating systems are optimized to handle multiple concurrent client requests efficiently. They emphasize stability, security, and resource management for services like web hosting and databases.

questions.question: What feature is most critical in mobile operating systems?
questions.explanation: Power management and battery efficiency are critical in mobile OS because mobile devices run on limited battery power. The OS must balance performance with energy consumption to extend battery life.

questions.question: In a multiprocessor operating system, what is symmetric multiprocessing?
options: All processors share equal access to memory and I/O
Processors work on different operating systems
questions.explanation: Symmetric multiprocessing means all processors share equal access to memory and I/O devices. Any processor can run any task, and the OS distributes work evenly across all processors.

questions.question: Which operating system type is best suited for applications where timing predictability is more important than throughput?
questions.explanation: Real-time operating systems prioritize timing predictability over throughput. They ensure tasks complete within specified time constraints, which is critical for control systems and embedded applications.

questions.question: What technique keeps several programs in memory at once to raise CPU utilization?
questions.explanation: Multiprogramming keeps multiple jobs in memory so the CPU switches to another when one waits for I/O. It reduces idle time.

questions.question: What is the fixed CPU time slice per process in a time-sharing system called?
questions.explanation: The time quantum is the slice each process receives before preemption. Short quanta give responsive interactive sharing.

questions.question: What OS type permits only one user at a time?
questions.explanation: Single-user systems serve one person at a time, like early PC operating systems. They lack multi-user access controls.

questions.question: What is an operating system called when it runs inside a virtual machine?
questions.explanation: A guest OS runs on virtualized hardware presented by a hypervisor. The host manages the physical machine beneath it.

questions.question: What software layer creates and manages virtual machines?
questions.explanation: A hypervisor, or virtual machine monitor, allocates hardware among VMs. It isolates guests from each other.

questions.question: What hypervisor type runs directly on the hardware?
questions.explanation: Type 1 hypervisors run on bare metal without a host OS. Examples include VMware ESXi and Microsoft Hyper-V.

questions.question: What hypervisor type runs as an application on a conventional host OS?
questions.explanation: Type 2 hypervisors run as hosted applications atop an existing OS. VirtualBox and VMware Workstation are examples.

questions.question: What real-time category tolerates occasional missed deadlines?
questions.explanation: Soft real-time systems degrade gracefully when deadlines slip. Video streaming is a typical example.

questions.question: What capability lets smartphones keep several apps active concurrently?
questions.explanation: Mobile OSs multitask by rapidly switching between apps. Background apps are suspended to save power.

questions.question: What OS type powers supercomputers running large parallel computations?
questions.explanation: Parallel operating systems coordinate thousands of processors on shared computations. They handle partitioning and synchronization at massive scale.

questions.question: What is the primary user interface of mobile operating systems?
questions.explanation: Mobile OSs center on touch input with gestures and on-screen keyboards. Voice control supplements but does not replace touch.

questions.question: What kernel design runs most services in user space?
questions.explanation: Microkernels keep only minimal functions in kernel space and run drivers and file systems as user processes. This improves fault isolation.

questions.question: What kernel architecture places all OS services in kernel space?
questions.explanation: Monolithic kernels run all services in privileged mode, sharing address space. Linux is a classic example.

questions.question: What term describes processors sharing a common memory and clock?
questions.explanation: Tightly coupled processors share main memory and communicate through it. Loosely coupled systems pass messages over a network instead.

questions.question: What setup lets a computer choose among installed operating systems at startup?
questions.explanation: Dual boot installs multiple OSs on separate partitions. A boot menu selects which one loads at power-on.

questions.question: VxWorks and QNX are examples of which OS type?
questions.explanation: VxWorks and QNX are real-time operating systems. They guarantee deterministic response times for embedded control systems.

questions.question: A pacemaker's pacing pulse must arrive on schedule; a single missed deadline can be fatal. Which OS type is required?
questions.explanation: Hard real-time systems must guarantee every deadline; failure can be catastrophic, matching a pacemaker.

questions.question: One master processor runs the OS and assigns work to slave processors that have no scheduling autonomy. What is this arrangement?
questions.explanation: In asymmetric multiprocessing only the master executes OS code; slaves run assigned tasks, unlike SMP where any CPU can run the kernel.

questions.question: Which description best fits a grid computing system?
options: Heterogeneous resources spanning multiple administrative domains
questions.explanation: Grids federate heterogeneous, geographically dispersed resources owned by different organizations; clusters are homogeneous and co-located.

questions.question: Identical PCs on a dedicated LAN are managed so users and jobs see a single resource pool for parallel work. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Clusters are loosely coupled but homogeneous machines on one site, presenting a unified pool for high-availability or parallel computing.

questions.question: In a peer-to-peer system, each node typically acts as what?
questions.explanation: P2P nodes share and consume resources symmetrically, removing the dedicated-server bottleneck of client-server designs.
